chunks: And by this chain, from Anbasah, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Muhammad ibn Abdullah came up, greeted, and then went away. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sympathized with him, and his eyes shed tears. So I said to him: 'I have seen you do with him something you never used to do.' He said: 'I sympathized with him because he is attributed to a command that is not his; I did not find him in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) among the caliphs of this community, nor among its kings.'

key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali, referring to a specific text listing successors
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Muhammad ibn Abdullah, known as al-Nafs al-Zakiyya
key_terms.مُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ: Mu'alla ibn Khunays, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq weep for Muhammad ibn Abdullah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) wept for Muhammad ibn Abdullah (al-Nafs al-Zakiyya) due to his impending revolt, which, though popular, lacked the divine designation (Ismah) of the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam clarifies that Muhammad was not among the true caliphs or kings recorded in the 'Book of Ali' (Kitab Ali), distinguishing his political uprising from the legitimate, divinely ordained succession of the Imams.
